entities.summary:
Domnall Brecc was the king of Dál Riata in medieval Scotland, ruling from approximately 629 to 642 CE. He was the son of Eochaid Buide and succeeded his brother, Eochaid's son, as king.

Brecc's reign was marked by the continued struggle between the Picts and the Dal Riata for control of Scotland. He also faced challenges from the Vikings, who were raiding the coastal areas.

Brecc's legacy is tied to the succession crisis that followed his death, which led to the eventual rise of the Kingdom of Scotland.

Domnall Brecc died in 642 CE, and his legacy was cemented by the scholar Fraxinius, who referred to him as Donald II of Scotland.

The Dál Riata kingdom's influence extended to the Isle of Man, where Brecc's descendants continued to rule until the 10th century.

The legacy of Domnall Brecc can also be seen in the modern-day cultural heritage of Scotland, where his name and legacy are still celebrated today.
